Rating: 8/10 — I hate this game. I also can't stop playing it.

Dota 2 is one of the greatest games ever made.

It is also one of the most mentally exhausting, rage-inducing, time-consuming pieces of ♥♥♥♥ you can voluntarily install on your computer.

And somehow, both things are true.

The first thing you need to understand about Dota 2 is that this isn't a game you casually play.

You don't "play one game."

You play one game, lose because your mid died three times before minute 10, tell yourself "okay, last game."

Then you queue again.

You lose again.

Now you're angry.

So naturally, you queue for another game because apparently the solution to losing Dota is more Dota.

The Good

When Dota 2 works, it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beautiful.

There is an absurd amount of depth in this game. Hundreds of heroes, ridiculous item combinations, positioning, timings, map control, farming patterns, vision, counter-picks, spell interactions and team coordination.

A single decision can completely change a game.

You can be getting destroyed for 30 minutes and suddenly find one perfect team fight.

One Ravage.

One Chronosphere.

One Black Hole.

One perfectly timed save.

One buyback.

Suddenly the enemy's entire advantage disappears.

That feeling is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incredible.

Few multiplayer games can give you that kind of satisfaction.

And the best part?

There isn't always one correct way to win.

You can split push.

You can team fight.

You can rat.

You can snowball.

You can turtle high ground for 40 minutes and somehow turn the game around.

You can completely change your hero's role depending on the situation.

That's what makes Dota special.

The Bad

Now let's talk about the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

The community.

♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

Dota players can turn a perfectly normal game into a psychological warfare simulator.

Someone dies once:

"MID DIFF."

Someone misses one spell:

"REPORT SUPPORT."

Your carry doesn't like your item choice:

"NOOB."

Someone disconnects:

"GG."

And somehow, after 15 minutes of everyone flaming each other, the team still has to coordinate a five-man smoke.

It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous.

And let's not pretend we're innocent.

We've all been that guy.

We've all typed something we immediately regretted.

We've all blamed someone else for a loss.

We've all said:

"If my team wasn't garbage, we would've won."

Would I recommend it?

Yes.

Would I recommend it to my worst enemy?

Absolutely.

Because apparently I don't want them to be happy either.

Офіційно можу заявити, що це НАЙГІРША МОБА гра яку можна уявити, як мінімум з боку новачка.

З самого початку гра зустрічає тебе різноманіттям героїв, це чудово, але це плюс і мінус. Ти можеш обрати будь кого, але при цьому ти не знаєш кого обирати, бо вибір неймовірний. Для мене це було складно, але це не основний мінус гри. Це нюанс.

Інтерфейс? Інтерфейс головного меню робили криві ідіоти, тому що на початку він відчувається контрінтуїтивним і вимагає тупо шукати деякі функції, які здавалось би мали лежати на поверхні. До цього можна звикнути, але враження псує жахливо.

МАТЧМЕЙКІНГ І СИСТЕМА ПОКАРАНЬ. Ось так, оце чудово, це неймовірно, це просто СЮР. Ти новачок, у тебе умовно 11 годин. Гра матч за матчем систематично може кидати тебе до людини у якої ТИСЯЧІ годин у цій прошу вибачення ПОМИЙЦІ. Очевидно, що людина на досвіді, практично в соло розфармлюється на новачках що з радістю фідять задроту і матч за матчем це призводить до того, що матчі зливаються. Це не поодинокі випадки, це систематична проблема. 

Я з горющєй попай почав лівати з матчів, де такі без перебільшення пси портять гру, і очікувано отримав низький приорітет і обмеження режимів ЯКІ ВЗАГАЛІ НЕ ПРОЕКТУВАЛИСЬ ДЛЯ НОВАЧКІВ. Уявіть, ви людина яка знає +- адекватно дай бог 1 героя, і вас щоб отримати доступ до звичайних ігор змушують грати у Single Draft, де ви щоматчу маєте обрати 1 з декількох випадкових героїв. Це призводить до ситуацій, коли вам дають вибір між пачкою абсолютно невідомих вам персонажів. 

При цьому, проблема матчмейкінгу НІКУДИ не зникла, вам все ще падають задроти з тисячами годин, але тепер ви вимушені грати на невідомих вам персонажах проти задрота. Одна справа, якби умова була у тому, щоб просто ЗІГРАТИ ці матчі, НІІІ, гра змушує вас ПЕРЕМОГТИ. Я за свої 11 годин переміг лише від сили 3 рази, може 4. Я не скіловий гравець і близько і це визнаю. Але в таких умовах, які ставить гра просто НЕМОЖЛИВО вийти з бану, бо гра робить усе, щоб ти як новачок не міг ПЕРЕМОГТИ.

Я вперше пишу настільки гнівний відгук на гру, бо ніяка гра, крім цієї ще невикликала у мене стільки ненависті до розробників. Якщо ви ніколи в це не грали, прошу вас І НЕ ГРАЙТЕ, це зекономить вам купу нервів і сил, а головне ЧАСУ. Шкодую за втрачені 11 годин.

Almost 900 hours in Dota 2, mostly playing solo but also quite a bit with friends over the years.

One thing I've always liked about this game is the number of heroes you can choose from. There's so much variety that even after hundreds of hours you can still try a different hero, role or playstyle and have a completely different experience.

I also remember playing back around 2016-2017 and when I compare that Dota to what we have now, A LOT has changed. New heroes, new mechanics, map changes and so many other updates have been added over the years. It's actually pretty crazy looking back at how different the game used to be.

Gameplay is still really good, graphics hold up well and there's always something new to learn.

Of course, some matches will make you question why you even opened the game in the first place 😂 but then you'll queue for another one anyway.

900 hours later... definitely recommended.

In a vacuum Dota is the best game ever made. Valve decided to make the game completely free. In a vacuum great idea. The sad truth is we do not live in a vacuum.
The game being free means that all smurfs, griefers, cheaters and every scum you can imagine can cheat their way up the ranks with impunity just by making another account.

The game being old is not really a factor here. Dota is that good. Valve on the other hand, not so much. They grew out bored of Dota and pretty much stopped its development. You get the occasional update which feels more and more that it has been written by an AI. You get a new hero every other year and the meta rots in place for months on end.

Related to the above, some game breaking bugs (seeing through the fog of war) are in the game for decades now. These bugs have been in the game so long they now are features being abused by high ranking players.

TLDR;
The game is awesome but riddled with bugs
The community is the worst
and Valve is a disgrace

Found this little indie game while looking for something to play with friends and honestly I'm surprised more people don't know about it.

You pick one of these cute little characters and then you and 9 other players spend some quality time together on a small map. The art is pretty charming and there's a surprising amount of attention to detail for such a tiny studio.

The gameplay is very simple. You just walk around, click on things and occasionally fight some of the local wildlife. There's also a little economy system where you collect gold and buy funny items for your character. Very cozy.

My favorite part is the community. Since this is such a small indie title, everyone seems to know each other. Every match feels like I'm sitting down with a few close friends for a relaxed evening. Sometimes we have disagreements about which direction to walk in, but that's just part of the wholesome co-op experience.

There are also hundreds of characters, which is honestly insane for a game this small. I've been playing for a while and still haven't seen everything. Some of them have really cute names like "Pudge" and "Techies."

The developer is clearly very passionate too. They keep releasing updates and adding new content despite the game being made by what I assume is like three people.

If you have 40 minutes to spare, definitely give this hidden gem a chance.

Would recommend.

Dota 2 is one of those games that makes you want to uninstall it, close Steam, and never play again… only to launch 
it again 10 minutes later.

Let’s start with the good.

In terms of gameplay depth, Dota 2 is genuinely one of the most impressive competitive games out there. The huge number of heroes, items, abilities, strategies, combinations, and possible builds makes every match potentially different. There is always something new to learn. Even after hundreds or thousands of hours, you can discover a new mechanic, a new strategy, an unusual build, or realize that you have been playing a hero completely wrong.

And that is exactly why the problems with the game can be so frustrating.

Dota 2 itself is incredibly good.

The problem is everything surrounding that gameplay.

The biggest issue is that one player can completely ruin a match for nine other people.

Someone dies twice in the first few minutes and immediately decides the game is over. Someone starts insulting the entire team. Someone refuses to cooperate. Someone spends 40 minutes farming the jungle while the rest of the team is desperately trying to defend the base. Someone makes one mistake and then spends the rest of the match explaining why everyone else is responsible for losing.

And somehow, the player with 5,000+ hours who is screaming at everyone about how terrible they are will usually make an even bigger mistake five minutes later.

Matchmaking can be another adventure by itself.

Sometimes you get an amazing match where both teams are evenly matched. Every fight matters, every tower matters, and one good decision can completely change the game. You get comebacks, smart rotations, team fights, Roshan contests, clutch saves and genuinely memorable moments.

Those are the games that remind you why Dota 2 is so addictive.

Then you get the opposite.

A completely one-sided match where the outcome is basically decided after 15 minutes, but somehow you still have to spend another 30 minutes watching your Ancient slowly disappear.

At that point you are sitting in front of your monitor thinking:

“Why am I still playing this?”

The match ends.

You click “Play Again.”

And that is probably the most accurate description of Dota 2.

It is a game that can make you angrier than almost anything else, yet somehow convinces you that the next match will be different.

Toxicity deserves its own section.

Dota 2 toxicity has become almost a fundamental part of the experience. Insults, spam pings, sarcastic voice lines, blaming supports for everything, blaming the carry, blaming the mid player, blaming the offlaner, blaming the draft, blaming the matchmaking…

Sometimes it feels like people don't actually queue to win.

They queue to find someone to blame when they lose.

The funniest part is that everyone thinks they are the main character.

Your carry thinks the support is useless.

The support thinks the carry is useless.

The mid player thinks both supports are useless.

The offlaner thinks the mid player ruined the game.

And the enemy team is somehow cheating.

Perfect teamwork.

There is also the problem of smurfs, boosters and unfair matches. Valve has taken measures against smurfing and has banned large numbers of accounts for this kind of behavior, which shows how serious the problem has been. But the fact that these issues have been such a major topic in the community says a lot about how important matchmaking integrity is for a competitive game like Dota 2.

Then there is the learning curve.

Dota 2 is not a game you simply install and understand.

For a new player, it can feel like being thrown into a university exam without ever attending the classes.

There are dozens of heroes to learn, hundreds of items, different roles, abilities, counters, timings, farming patterns, map movements, ward locations, objectives, Roshan timings and countless small mechanics that experienced players take for granted.

A new player can spend hours learning the basics and then meet someone who understands the game far better and gets destroyed in seconds.

The experienced player thinks:

“Easy.”

The new player thinks:

“What the hell just happened?”

But once you finally understand the basics, something changes.

You start seeing the game differently.

You stop simply reacting to things and start predicting them.

You understand why the enemy is moving somewhere. You recognize a potential gank. You know when to fight and when to retreat. You start thinking about item timings, map control, objectives and positioning.

And that is when Dota 2 becomes truly amazing.

Few things feel better than winning a difficult match because your team actually worked together.

A perfectly executed team fight.

A last-second save.

A successful smoke gank.

Stealing Roshan.

Defending your high ground for 20 minutes.

Turning a completely lost game into a comeback.

Those moments are incredible.

And those moments are exactly why people keep coming back.

Dota 2 is not a bad game.

Actually, the opposite is true.

It is an incredibly good game surrounded by an incredible amount of frustration.

Gameplay: 10/10.

Depth: 10/10.

Variety: 10/10.

Teamwork: 10/10 — when your team actually works together.

Learning curve: Pain.

Matchmaking: Sometimes a lottery.

Toxicity: Basically its own game mode.

Amount of time you can lose: Unlimited.

Dota 2 is one of those games where you completely understand why people love it while also completely understanding why they hate it.

You can have the best match of your life and immediately follow it with the worst match imaginable.

You can spend an hour playing perfectly, lose because of one stupid decision, stare at the defeat screen for a few seconds and say:

“That's it. I'm done with Dota.”

Then five minutes later:

“Okay, one more.”

And that's the Dota 2 experience.

I recommend it to anyone who enjoys extremely deep competitive games and is willing to spend hundreds of hours learning, losing, improving, getting tilted, recovering, and occasionally experiencing one of the most satisfying victories a multiplayer game can offer.

For everyone else…

Stay away.

I came back to Dota 2 after not playing since 2018, and I honestly can't believe how far the game has fallen.

The current report and punishment system is absurd. Players can report you simply because they don't like the way you played, the hero you picked, a decision you made, or because they need someone to blame for losing. In a competitive game, disagreements and mistakes are inevitable, yet the system gives other players far too much influence over whether you are allowed to continue playing.

I'm convinced that even professional Champions League-level players could join regular matchmaking and still get reported by random teammates who think they know better.

After 1,500+ hours, I also see absolutely no reason to spend money on Dota anymore. Why buy expensive skins or support the game financially when a few angry players can report you and you can end up unable to play? You can literally have hundreds of euros worth of cosmetics on an account and still have your evening ruined because some random kids decided they didn't like how you played.

Dota used to be a game I could recommend. In its current state, I can't.
